dreaddit.title: Dreaddit
dreaddit.source_title: Dreaddit: A Reddit Dataset for Stress Analysis in Social Media
dreaddit.source_unit: A labeled segment of a Reddit post, not an entire clinical case or participant interview.
dreaddit.background: The original corpus supports stress identification in social-media language. Its stress labels are not annotations of flaws in qualitative claims.
dreaddit.experiment_use: The n100 experiment uses development_train records from the local deidentified records.jsonl, ultimately derived from dreaddit-train.csv. The 580-packet bank selects eligible records in record-ID order, with distinct post source IDs, and groups four excerpts per packet. The balanced subset takes 20 packet IDs per intended flaw. Official test data are not in this n100 set.
dreaddit.context_limit: The packet contains the selected segment, not the complete Reddit post or thread. The sentence range is available in upstream analysis-record provenance but not in the historical packet's local_context field.
dreaddit.interpretation: This corpus can motivate evidence-grounded interpretation of stress narratives. It cannot establish clinical validity, stress diagnosis, or expert adjudication of the injected claims.
dreaddit.preparation: Analysis records mask URLs, email addresses and user handles where detected. Exact text can remain searchable. Catalog verification is against the prepared analysis text, not a claim of byte-for-byte identity with unmasked CSV text.

goemotions.title: GoEmotions
goemotions.source_title: GoEmotions: A Dataset of Fine-Grained Emotions
goemotions.source_unit: One Reddit comment in the official simplified train.tsv split.
goemotions.background: The original annotation task uses 27 emotion categories plus neutral. These labels describe emotion, not flaws in a generated review or claim. The table sometimes uses the singular alias GoEmotion; the official dataset name is GoEmotions.
goemotions.experiment_use: The working bank uses train.tsv, not the full-dataset CSVs. It keeps comments of at least five words, normalizes whitespace, preserves eligible row order and groups four comments per packet. The bank has 9,540 prepared packets; only its balanced n100 subset has stored reviewer outputs in this catalog. The official dev and test splits are not in that n100 set.
goemotions.context_limit: The simplified file does not supply surrounding conversations. Four comments in a packet are not evidence of a single thread, common author or naturally coherent discussion.
goemotions.interpretation: This source motivates examining whether emotional interpretations remain faithful to short utterances. Original emotion labels cannot serve as gold labels for the five experimental flaw categories.
goemotions.preparation: The builder normalizes whitespace. The catalog maps each source_record_id to the exact TSV row and records original emotion IDs separately. Comment identifiers are hashed in provenance, not exposed as author identities.

agyw_focus_groups.title: CaChe
agyw_focus_groups.source_title: Cache2 Focus Group Discussion Transcripts AGYW and Community Males
agyw_focus_groups.source_unit: An eligible participant turn in one of 11 focus-group transcript files. A turn is not a unique person.
agyw_focus_groups.background: The source deposit concerns adolescent girls and young women and community men, with discussion of the COVID-19 pandemic, relationships and health in rural western Kenya. English analysis text includes English source passages and English translations. This description is supported by the local source manifest; the repository page could not be refreshed during this catalog build.
agyw_focus_groups.experiment_use: The working bank uses eligible turns from the deidentified records.jsonl, interleaving focus groups and grouping four turns per packet. The bank contains 765 prepared packets. The main balanced n100 contains 400 distinct turn records spanning all 11 source FGDs. The internal corpus ID remains agyw_focus_groups.
agyw_focus_groups.context_limit: Moderator-question context and preceding-record IDs may be present. IDs alone are not the text of those previous turns. Excerpts can come from different FGDs and must not be narrated as one continuous exchange.
agyw_focus_groups.interpretation: This material supports discussing contextual sensitivity and grounded qualitative interpretation. It does not provide independently verified flaw labels for the newly constructed claims. The historical heldout_cross_domain_evaluation label is not evidence that these already-used records remain untouched holdout data.
agyw_focus_groups.preparation: The source is participant-numbered and selectively redacted, not guaranteed anonymous. The local manifest records filename/date inconsistencies and secondary-use review requirements. Exact text stays restricted locally; catalog construction is not clearance for public release or external model processing.

parlamint_gb.title: ParlaMint-GB
parlamint_gb.citation: ParlaMint project, CLARIN.SI handle 11356/1486; Erjavec et al., The ParlaMint corpora of parliamentary proceedings
parlamint_gb.source_unit: A speaker turn in a TEI XML parliamentary session, with the source session and speaker retained.
parlamint_gb.background: The local ParlaMint-GB archive covers public parliamentary proceedings from the Commons and Lords. Version and origin are recorded in the local provenance document; the repository page could not be refreshed during this catalog build.
parlamint_gb.experiment_use: The full-sample builder retains turns of 8 to 800 words, producing a recorded eligible pool of 607,907 turns. It samples 400 turns with random seed 20260901, sorts the draw by year/chamber/source/record, and forms 100 packets. The main n100 comprises all 100 packets in this bank, with 400 turns from 352 distinct session source IDs.
parlamint_gb.context_limit: Each excerpt is a single turn, not the full debate. A packet may combine unrelated debates. The catalog resolves each selected text and speaker to its original archive member and XML utterance ID without unpacking the archive.
parlamint_gb.interpretation: This corpus supports examining evidence-grounded interpretation of institutional policy discourse. The local packet construction does not turn parliamentary text into a human-adjudicated flaw benchmark. Sorting before sequential flaw allocation can associate flaw groups with time or chamber and should be considered in future design.
parlamint_gb.preparation: The builder joins XML segment text and normalizes whitespace. The historical heldout_cross_domain_descriptive split label is retained as history, not a new assurance of unseen evaluation data. This is the British component, not the complete multinational ParlaMint collection.
